## Remaining first-render cost

Three production profiles of the final candidate put the median active browser time at 37.63 ms under the profiler. The median self time is 6.33 ms in core orchestration, 5.49 ms in native main-thread work, 3.36 ms in layout and formatting, 2.58 ms in DOM code (including 1.66 ms in the interaction module), 2.01 ms in theme resolution, 1.64 ms in scales and view, 1.22 ms in normalization, 1.20 ms in drawing, 1.02 ms in reader work and 0.76 ms in scene construction. Another 10.02 ms is unattributed JavaScript, including harness work. The browser's accessibility tree has no isolated time in these samples. The on-demand tooltip and table rendering have no distinct sampled cost. The active compact profile attributes 11.47 ms to theme work across 40 charts. The remaining work to reach 10 ms would include eliminating forced style and layout reads across chart creation, reducing first-use locale formatting, and deferring interaction setup that can safely wait for first focus or input. Those changes need separate prototypes and profiles. The generated description, synchronous diagnostics and first-frame drawing are required behaviors. The sampled costs do not establish that those changes alone could save 17.40 ms.

Proposal for the owner: set the 1.0 P1 budget to 30 ms for the same workload and reference desktop. The candidate recorded 27.40 ms in 20 runs, giving 2.60 ms of margin. # Working in this repository

Axylo is a browser charting library. The product is specified in `docs/02-product-spec.md`; the build plan is `docs/03-plan-typescript-release.md`. Read the sections your task names before writing code.

## Rules for every change

- **Contracts are fixed.** `packages/axylo/src/core/contracts.ts` and `packages/axylo/src/public.ts` are the interfaces between modules. Do not edit them. If your work needs a change there, stop that part, finish what you can, and describe the exact change you need in your report.
- **Stay in your files.** Each task lists the directories it owns. Do not create, edit or delete anything else, including configuration and other modules. Several agents work in this checkout at the same time.
- **No runtime dependencies.** Use the platform (`Intl`, typed arrays). Dev dependencies already installed: TypeScript, Vitest, fast-check, esbuild, Playwright (system Chrome), axe-core. The network is not available; do not try to install anything.
- **No DOM at import time.** A module that needs the DOM takes it as a parameter or touches it inside a function. Pure stages (data, scales, formatting, layout, scene) must run in Node.
- **Hot paths use typed arrays.** No object per data point, no array of arrays per data point, no copying of large columns that the contracts say are borrowed.
- **Never guess silently.** Anything that cannot be drawn as given is reported through the `DiagnosticSink` with the code from spec section 3.5.
- **Tests come from the spec.** Expected values are derived from the specification and the fixture data, never by running the implementation and pasting its output. Use fast-check property tests for invariants ("for any data …"). A test you cannot make pass is reported as failing; do not weaken it or change its expected value.
- **TypeScript strict, no `any`** in exported signatures. `__DEV__` is a build-time boolean (true in tests).
- **Comments say why**, not what. Names are plain words.
- **Do not commit.** The coordinator commits.

## Commands

```bash
npm run typecheck      # tsc over the library, its tests, and the API examples in docs/api
npm test               # unit and property tests (Node)
npm run build          # packages/axylo/dist
npm run test:browser   # browser tests against the built bundle, in system Chrome
```

End with a short report: what you built (files), what you verified and how (paste the last lines of the test run), what is not done or not verified, any contract change you need, and any place where the spec was ambiguous and what you assumed. Keep "ran and saw" apart from "expect".

Architecture ### 2.1 Pipeline ``` options ─► normalize ─► frame ──┬─► view model ─► layout ─► scene ─► mark renderer │ validate (authoritative) │ scales, visible range text renderer (DOM) ▼ diagnostics ├─► lookup: exact values by x, by point, by ordinal ├─► summary and table └─► focus model ``` The **frame** is the normalized, lossless data: typed columns, a validity bitmap, dictionary-encoded categories, source-row indexes and a revision number. It is the only source for exact values. The table, the summary, keyboard navigation, tooltips and events read the frame. The **scene** is geometry for drawing and may be simplified (F5); nothing reads values back from it. The first draft derived accessibility from the scene, and two reviewers showed that a simplified drawing cannot return the samples it dropped. | Stage | Output | Notes | |---|---|---| | normalize | Frame, diagnostics | The only place raw input is read. Never coerces silently. | | view model | Scales, visible index ranges, series visibility | Domain rules implement F1 and F7. | | lookup | Nearest-x by binary search; nearest-point by a grid index (scatter) | Works on the frame within the visible range; cost bounded independently of the drawing. | | layout | Plot rectangle, tick sets, label boxes, legend and control placement | Implements L1, L3, L8. Takes a text-measurement interface as input. | | scene | Flat list of primitives (`path`, `rect`, `arc`, `rule`, `text`) | Plain data; testable in Node with injected text metrics. | | renderers | Marks; DOM text; accessibility DOM | See 2.3. | ### 2.2 Invalidation Stages are cached, and the cache keys are explicit. Caching on object identity alone, as the first draft said, would miss font loads, pixel-ratio changes and in-place mutation. | Stage | Reruns when | |---|---| | normalize | Data revision or field encoding changes. `append` extends the frame without renormalizing earlier rows. | | view model | Frame revision, zoom, series visibility, author domains. | | layout | View model; container size; resolved font and text spacing; `document.fonts` finishing a load; locale; any label text. A data-only update reruns layout when the tick labels would change, and skips it otherwise. | | scene | Layout or view model. | | mark raster | Scene; device pixel ratio; resolved colors (L4's triggers). | Text is measured with the page's computed font, letter spacing and word spacing applied to the measuring context, and layout reruns when fonts finish loading. The measurement interface is a parameter, so Node tests inject fixed metrics and browser tests use the real one. ### 2.3 Rendering **Working assumption: Canvas 2D for marks, HTML for all text.** Text stays in the DOM so that it inherits the page font and color, honors user text spacing and zoom (A6), adapts in forced-colors mode, and can be selected and translated. **This is reopened and decided in M1 by measurement.** The first draft justified canvas by Phase 1's slow SVG libraries, but those create a node per point; the one-path-per-series SVG chart in the harness was fast. With drawing simplified to a few vertices per pixel column (F5), an SVG path per series is small. SVG follows CSS variables and class-toggled themes with no repaint code, adapts to forced colors, prints sharply, needs no pixel-ratio handling and allocates no backing store (a 1,920×1,080 canvas at pixel ratio 2 is about 33 MB). Canvas is likely cheaper for per-frame redraw when streaming and hovering. M1 builds both mark renderers behind the same scene and compares them on: P1, P2, P3, P5, bytes, memory, a runtime theme toggle, forced colors, print, and browser zoom. The scene is renderer-neutral either way, so the choice is contained. **Simplified drawing.** Per device-pixel column and per contiguous run of valid samples, the stroke covers the run's minimum and maximum (F5).
